name: skye-elements-registry
purpose: Composable design elements for Skye/Spectacle MCP generation. Elements are referenced by namespace so sources can be combined without turning into a Frankenstein page.

compositionPolicy.rule: Use one primary visual language per page, then add supporting elements only when they serve the same story.
forbidden: Mixing unrelated hero styles from multiple products
Using an asset because it exists instead of because it clarifies the offer
Stacking every animation library on one page
Combining dark luxury, playful SaaS, brutalist, and app UI styles in the same viewport
Treating screenshots, logos, and 3D objects as interchangeable decorations
Claiming advanced open-source tooling without real imports
Reusing the same dark card/dashboard template with a different brand name
required: Run design_stack_audit when advanced tooling is required
Run design_performance_audit when advanced motion, WebGL, screenshots, or scroll effects are used

namespaces.skye.core: Foundational Skye/Spectacle palette, typography, spacing, and proof language.
namespaces.skye.fx: Premium cursor, scrollbar, neon text, shimmer, and interaction polish.
namespaces.skye.proof: Client-safe proof panels and operator evidence patterns.
namespaces.skye.brand: Logo, wordmark, identity asset discipline, and anti-generic-brand rules.
namespaces.skyesol.reference: Read-only extracted SkyeSol assets and style notes.
namespaces.client.surface: App-first surfaces, dashboards, command centers, and control panels.

elements.description: A wide first viewport with headline across the page, short support copy, obvious CTA, and one command-surface visual.
elements.useWhen: The product needs a premium first impression and must avoid left-column text walls.

elements.description: The app/tool UI is the first screen, with real controls, tabs, status, and workflow density.
elements.useWhen: The user asked for an app, dashboard, database command center, editor, game, or internal tool.

elements.description: A restrained WebGL/Three.js ambient scene: particles, depth, glow, camera parallax, and product symbolism.
elements.useWhen: The product benefits from a sense of living infrastructure or spatial control.

elements.description: A scroll-led story that stages signup, setup, proof, handoff, and conversion with one clear action per stage.
elements.useWhen: A buyer must understand a process or trust path before signup.

elements.description: Client-safe trust evidence: checks, receipts, status, timestamps, proof labels, and handoff state.
elements.useWhen: The page needs proof without exposing internal smoke logs or raw debug output.

elements.description: Transparent founder media staged as an authority object, paired with proof metrics and editorial copy.
elements.useWhen: Founder/operator trust is part of the sale.

elements.description: Subtle entrance, hover, and section reveal motion with reduced-motion fallback.
elements.useWhen: Almost every premium page, unless motion is disabled.

elements.description: Pointer-reactive glow/cursor trail for premium pages, with mobile and reduced-motion fallback.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for cursor trail, high-end interaction polish, or spectacle feel.

elements.description: Thicker branded scrollbar with an always-visible, slightly opaque neon track and glowing thumb treatment for scroll-led experiences.
elements.useWhen: The page is a long cinematic scroll or the user asks for a visible custom scrollbar.

elements.description: Full-page premium browser chrome: Legal Skyes-style neon scrollbar, top scroll progress rail, pointer-reactive glow, scanline texture, shimmer text, and magnetic hover utility classes.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for the legal page scrollbar style, stronger motion polish, neon UI chrome, scroll-progress feedback, or a page that should feel designed instead of merely styled.

elements.description: Glow, shimmer, split-line, reveal, or chromatic text treatments used as hierarchy, not clutter.
elements.useWhen: The art direction needs neon/glowing/premium display text effects.

elements.description: Use browser/app/product screenshots as the actual visual subject when the surface itself matters.
elements.useWhen: The product has a real app, dashboard, website, or generated surface that needs to be shown.

elements.description: A real MP4/WebM reel recorded from actual browser/app workflows and rendered as the first proof subject.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for screenshots animated into video-style proof, the surface needs to feel live, or the copy claims the app does a workflow.

elements.description: Use approved logo, mark, emblem, and wordmark assets before inventing any new mark.
elements.useWhen: Every branded public page, nav, hero, favicon, app shell, or client surface.

elements.description: Desktop/mobile browser screenshots, no mobile horizontal scroll, visible subject, visible CTA, clean public copy.
elements.useWhen: Every generated public page or app surface.
